content: As concerning as this sounds, The Netherlands is not a landlocked country nor a poor one. Desalination plants are a thing. The main issue is ground water levels. Due to large parts of the Netherlands being built on former swamp land, if the ground water levels fall too low it will have catastrophic effects on foundations of houses. Already in 2020 a report was released that 1/10th of all buildings in the Netherlands were at risk of foundational damage due to low ground water damage The actual problem isn't a drinking water shortage (well of course it is partially, but like you pointed out there are solutions for that). The biggest problem is that low ground water levels allow for salinization of the soil. This happens in two ways. Seawater can penetrate farther inland through rivers and estuaries because there is less freshwater flowing downstream to push it back. This salt part of the river is called "salt tongue" in Dutch. Under normal circumstances this stretches about 14km inland.
